title: Diskless Linux boot using ZFS, iSCSI and PXE
summary: A comprehensive guide on setting up diskless Linux boot infrastructure using ZFS for network-attached storage, iSCSI for block-level data transfer, and PXE for network boot initialization, enabling workstations to boot entirely over the network without local storage.
problem_solved: Enables diskless computing by allowing machines to boot and run Linux entirely from network storage, eliminating the need for local hard drives.
why_valuable: Provides a complete infrastructure solution for centralized system management, thin clients, and reduced hardware costs in enterprise environments.
